name: Lowdown menu
description: Lowdown records what MCP Registry servers declare and what is observed about them, daily, as dated facts (no scores). Call the lookup with ?menu=<name> to get only the part that answers your question. Without menu you get everything. No authentication.

sets.question: Should I install or connect this MCP server? Facts to decide before installing.
sets.contains: status, packages, declared-vs-observed, content-flags (and stdio results when published)

sets.question: What changed recently on this server?
sets.contains: tools, content-flags, declared-vs-observed, registry changes (30 days)

dishes.question: Does this MCP server answer right now, and does it require authentication?
dishes.contains: status, scanner.latest (latest probe: reach level, HTTP status, latency — one location, once a day)

dishes.question: Are the npm or PyPI packages it declares deprecated, yanked, archived, or gone (404)?
Did its tool definitions change, when, and with or without a server version change?
Does what the MCP Registry declares (version, hosts) match what is observed?
Did a tool definition change add a URL or invisible characters?
Which tools does it expose, without connecting to it?
What does the official MCP Registry declare, and what changed there in 30 days?
What happened on each of the last 30 days?
What did agents report after using it?
dishes.contains: interactions, success_rate, confidence and related fields (few external reports so far)

find.question: Which MCP servers match given conditions (answered without credentials, tool count, tool list unchanged for N days, Registry or package state)?
find.contains: matching servers with the values used to filter and sort, each with its lookup URL; the chosen sort key is the only order (no ranking)

also.name: compare_tools
also.question: How do several tools compare on agent-reported outcomes?

also.name: daily dataset
also.question: Records for many servers at once (CC BY 4.0).

planned.what: Results of installing the declared npm or PyPI package in an isolated sandbox and running initialize and tools/list over stdio.
Rule-based notable facts (for example a deprecated package, or tool definitions that changed without a server version change), with the rule and the evidence. No scores.
planned.status: recorded privately; publication criteria not decided yet

planned.what: Many servers and history longer than 30 days in one request (the raw daily data stays free in the public dataset).

body.missing: list of: stdio_results, risk_facts, longer_history, more_servers, alerts, faster_response, other
